key_insight: The 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination and chemical composition, with interface-induced polarization strongly shifting the local electrostatic landscape.
engineering_relevance: These results help guide interface engineering in perovskite solar cells by showing how passivating 2D layers can alter work function and band offsets, affecting charge extraction and stability.
method: Atomistic first-principles simulations using hybrid functionals
Modeled (PEA)2PbI4 / 3D perovskite interfaces with different terminations and compositions
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across layers
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary calculated shifts in valence band offsets of about 0.2 to 0.7 eV and conduction offsets of about 0.25 eV, depending on termination and chemistry.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and depend on specific surface cleavages and modeled compositions, so broader device-level performance implications still need validation.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
